rules.statement: A method that serializes to UTF-8 (JSON or otherwise) writes into a caller-supplied `IBufferWriter<byte>` (or a `Utf8JsonWriter`) and does not return a freshly allocated `byte[]`.
rules.why: Returning a `byte[]` goes against the buffer convention: callers should control where the output goes so no intermediate array gets allocated.
rules.check: Look for new public or internal methods that return `byte[]` from serialization, such as `SerializeToUtf8Bytes` or `ToArray()` results, where a buffer-writer overload should be offered instead.

rules.statement: When code needs a temporary buffer for serialized output, for example to parse it again or feed it to a log or span projection, rent a pooled buffer writer (`BufferFactory.CreatePooledBufferWriter` from `NCode.Buffers`) inside a `using` instead of allocating an array.
rules.why: Pooled buffers mean the intermediate step allocates no array.
rules.check: Look for intermediate `byte[]`, `MemoryStream.ToArray()` or `ArrayBufferWriter` used only as scratch space between writing and reading serialized data.

rules.statement: A method that accepts a buffer-writer destination declares it as a generic `ref TWriter destination` with `where TWriter : IBufferWriter<byte>, allows ref struct`, so that ref-struct writers are supported.
rules.why: This is the standard producer shape. It lets callers pass stack-only writers, even when the method has to stage the output internally, for example because `Utf8JsonWriter` can't hold a ref struct.
rules.check: Look for new methods that take a plain `IBufferWriter<byte>` parameter as their output destination instead of the generic `ref TWriter … allows ref struct` form.

rules.statement: Order write and copy method parameters with the source or input first and the destination (writer, buffer writer, output span) last.
rules.why: This keeps the codebase consistent with existing APIs such as `Decode(ciphertext, ref destination)` and `CopyPlaintext(source, destination)`.
rules.check: Look for new methods whose `Utf8JsonWriter`, `IBufferWriter<byte>`, `Span<byte>` or other destination parameter comes before the value being written.

rules.statement: Parse JSON with `JsonElement.Parse` rather than `JsonDocument.Parse` in new code.
rules.why: The maintainer wants to move off the older JSON parsing APIs. `JsonElement.Parse` leaves no disposable document to own.
rules.check: Look for new `JsonDocument.Parse` (or `JsonDocument.ParseValue`) calls in the diff where `JsonElement.Parse` would do.

rules.statement: Don't add a parameter for a value that can be derived from `HttpContext`, such as the endpoint name: derive it inside the method from `HttpContext.GetEndpoint()` metadata (`IEndpointNameMetadata.EndpointName`, else `DisplayName`).
rules.why: Passing a value the method can already derive from its context is redundant and lets callers drift from the one rule for deriving it.
rules.check: Look for methods that take both an `HttpContext` and a separate endpoint-name (or similar request-derived) argument, or for duplicated helper code that reads endpoint metadata.
